title: N-Queens
prompt:
Place `n` queens on an `n×n` chessboard so that no two queens attack each other (no shared row, column, or diagonal). Return all distinct solutions, in any order. Each solution is a list of rows, with `'Q'` for a queen and `'.'` for an empty square.

**Example**: `n = 4` → `[[".Q..","...Q","Q...","..Q."],["..Q.","Q...","...Q",".Q.."]]`.

**Constraints**: 1 ≤ n ≤ 9.
hints: No two queens can share a row, so each row gets exactly one queen. Before placing a queen in column c of row r, what must you check?
Backtrack row by row. For each column, skip it if that column or either diagonal through the square is already attacked; otherwise place the queen and recurse to the next row.

Squares on one ↘ diagonal share `r - c`; squares on one ↙ diagonal share `r + c`. Track `cols[c]`, `diag[r - c + n]` and `anti[r + c]`: set them before recursing and clear them after. At `row == n`, copy the board rows into strings.

solution.explanation: Placing one queen per row rules out row conflicts automatically. Every square on a diagonal has the same `r - c` or `r + c`, so three boolean arrays make each safety check O(1). Adding `n` keeps the `r - c` index non-negative. O(n!) time in the worst case, since the choices shrink row by row; O(n) extra space besides the output.
